comments.author: ivan-egorov42
comments.body:
@Graur I've explored the sources of java `string toLowerCase()` method and that's what I realized:
1) First of all, if we want to support all languges as  java `string toLowerCase()` then we need to use Unicode and implement some kind of "language" object where we can define encoding of a particular language(its range of symbols) and etc.
2) Second, we should work with characters, so we should be able to parse string for characters, then work with their hex representation.
3) Finally, we can't work with hex due to the lack of necessary method, change it, add and etc. Also, immutability doesn't allow to change capitals in process, so we have to use recursion for each symbol and it greatly limits the size of the text we can transform.

I don't think if we could have another implementation, this is how these methods are implemented in other languages. Here is [java example](https://www.javatpoint.com/java-string-tolowercase). For now, I see no reason to rewrite these methods via. EO as we don't have enough instruments for it. If somebody can give an idea for other solution, I will be very grateful. Also, I want to get feedback from you about my points of view.
